chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Miskan, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man speaking during the iqamah. He said: Yes. But when the mu'adhdhin says, “The salat has been established,” then speech becomes forbidden for the people of the mosque, unless they have gathered from different places and do not have an Imam; then there is no harm in some of them saying to another, “Go forward, O so-and-so.”

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the prayer leader for the congregation
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the iqamah, the second call announcing the immediate start of salat
key_terms.الْمُؤَذِّنُ: the one who gives the call to prayer
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: the phrase in the iqamah indicating that the salat has now been established

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the iqamah before congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling on speaking during the iqamah. Speaking is allowed generally during the iqamah, but once the mu'adhdhin says "qad qamati al-salat," speech becomes forbidden for those in the mosque, except when they need to appoint someone to lead the congregation.
